## Goal
- Repair Android APK signing/build failure, audit a fresh QA APK, and obtain evidence-backed emulator QA for production-aligned source.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Do not claim emulator QA, publication, deployment, production parity, or production-ready APK status without recorded successful evidence.
- Do not deploy application changes unless Android release build and emulator/Maestro QA pass.
- APKs signed with debug credentials must not be represented as Play Store/production-signing ready.
- Preserve owner authentication, source-mutation, Git push, deployment, emergency-stop, testing, and production-verification gates.
- Do not include incidental changes in release commits:
  ```text
  .rork/history/main/*.json
  expo/test-results/
  expo/playwright-report/
  ivx-holdings-platform
  ```

## Progress
### Done
- Corrected Playwright/Bun test-runner separation:
  - Renamed `expo/__tests__/e2e/ivx-owner-ai-smoke.spec.ts` to `expo/__tests__/e2e/ivx-owner-ai-smoke.e2e.ts`.
  - Added `expo/playwright.config.ts` with `testMatch: '**/*.e2e.ts'`.
  - Verified `bunx playwright test --list` discovers 3 tests.
- Rork source commit:
  ```text
  c57a0ff4cafa2c74f6748acf9dd267c3ff4b6be0
  Fixed issues with the automated testing system and updated the mobile application to the latest version.
  ```
- GitHub `main` and live production `/version` both reported:
  ```text
  362e7f5e4699ff8c013367901909f27a33857fa5
  ```
- Production public checks passed:
  ```text
  https://ivxholding.com HTTP 200
  https://api.ivxholding.com/health status: healthy
  /api/public/chat HTTP 200
  ```
- Public deterministic IVX IA response passed:
  ```json
  {
    "ok": true,
    "source": "fallback",
    "model": "ivx-ia-conversation-brain",
    "answer": "The answer is 56.",
    "error": null
  }
  ```
- Production Playwright smoke passed:
  ```bash
  cd expo && bunx playwright test --reporter=line
  ```
  ```text
  3 passed (4.0s)
  ```
- TypeScript check passed:
  ```bash
  bun x tsc --noEmit
  ```
- Existing APK static evidence:
  ```text
  path: expo/android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk
  package: com.ivxholdings.app
  versionCode: 91
  versionName: 1.9.3
  size: 84086875 bytes
  SHA-256: 72ea371eba36db79fa532b7a4dc3fd93288ed0519863473f974ba09e6c765a68
  ```
- Existing APK v2 signature verification passed structurally, but signer is debug-only:
  ```text
  CN=Android Debug, OU=Android, O=Unknown, L=Unknown, ST=Unknown, C=US
  ```
- Android QA GitHub Actions run was dispatched:
  ```text
  run: 30748881196
  job: 91499226677
  workflow: Android Release APK Build + Emulator QA
  head_sha: 362e7f5e4699ff8c013367901909f27a33857fa5
  ```
- Run `30748881196` completed as a failure:
  ```text
  started_at: 2026-08-02T12:56:41Z
  completed_at: 2026-08-02T13:05:28Z
  conclusion: failure
  ```
- Failure root cause was identified from workflow logs:
  ```text
  Execution failed for task ':app:packageRelease'.
  com.android.ide.common.signing.KeytoolException: Failed to read key androiddebugkey from store "/home/runner/work/ivx-holdings-platform/ivx-holdings-platform/expo/android/app/debug.keystore": DerInputStream.getLength(): lengthTag=63, too big.
  BUILD FAILED in 7m 44s
  ```
- Confirmed the repository copy of `expo/android/app/debug.keystore` at `362e7f5e…` is invalid:
  ```text
  /tmp/ivx-gh-debug.keystore: data
  keytool error: java.security.KeyStoreException: Unrecognized keystore format.
  ```
  ```text
  GitHub blob SHA: 6cbeb815cb9038bc1e6c4323848cc70209dd6221
  size: 3815
  SHA-256: 14e4e310d7c7037238ab569ecd66f150fcd0c12854f0de0e919c2def8ad4209c
  ```
- Local `expo/android/app/debug.keystore` is a valid Java KeyStore and differs from GitHub:
  ```text
  SHA-256: 221e0a3106aa4c3ccc154e0a418b55020b3f9ea6e84f92e8749cd9e2f39f5e58
  Alias: androiddebugkey
  SHA256: FA:C6:17:45:DC:09:03:78:6F:B9:ED:E6:2A:96:2B:39:9F:73:48:F0:BB:6F:89:9B:83:32:66:75:91:03:3B:9C
  ```
- Applied uncommitted signing repair:
  - `expo/android/app/build.gradle` no longer explicitly points `signingConfigs.debug` at tracked `expo/android/app/debug.keystore`.
  - It now relies on Android Gradle Plugin’s generated standard debug keystore for QA artifacts.
  - `.github/workflows/android-emulator-qa.yml` now validates/generates `$HOME/.android/debug.keystore` before `assembleRelease`.
- Workflow YAML validation passed:
  ```bash
  python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/android-emulator-qa.yml')); print('workflow YAML valid')"
  ```
- Confirmed no locally attached Android device/emulator:
  ```text
  List of devices attached
  ```
- Confirmed the 12 engineering IA roles are shared-worker role records, not independent autonomous runtimes:
  ```text
  total: 12
  real_independent: 0
  shared_worker: 12
  globalExecutionSlots: 1
  independentRuntimeCount: 0
  classification: SHARED_WORKER_WITH_ROLE
  ```

### In Progress
- Validate the modified Android signing configuration through a completed local `assembleRelease` result and APK inspection.
- Complete/retain final output from:
  ```bash
  cd expo/android && NODE_ENV=production ./gradlew assembleRelease --no-daemon -x lint
  cd expo && bun test --reporter dots
  ```
- Commit only intended signing/workflow changes, push them, and dispatch a replacement Android emulator QA run.
- Audit fresh APK metadata, SHA-256, signer, embedded bundle/source provenance, install, launch, Maestro, screenshot, and logcat evidence.

### Blocked
- Run `30748881196` never reached artifact upload, emulator installation, launch, Maestro, screenshot, or logcat QA because `:app:packageRelease` failed.
- The signing repair is currently uncommitted and not present on GitHub `main`; no replacement CI run can evidence it until committed/pushed.
- A valid QA debug signer is not an owner-controlled Play Store upload/release signer.
- Existing APK predates the required source changes and has no recorded proof it was built from production commit `362e7f5e…`; it cannot be called a verified-new-production APK.
- Protected owner endpoints remain inaccessible with available credentials:
  ```text
  /api/ivx/agent-audit/overview HTTP 401
  /api/ivx/autonomous/runs/summary HTTP 401
  /api/ivx/senior-developer/worker/status HTTP 401
  ```
- Provider proof remains incomplete; public chat succeeded through:
  ```text
  source: fallback
  model: ivx-ia-conversation-brain
  ```
- No local Android device is attached.

## Key Decisions
- Treat `30748881196` as failed, not slow/in-progress; its 7m44s duration was Android compilation before malformed tracked-keystore packaging failure.
- Remove dependence on tracked `expo/android/app/debug.keystore` for QA release builds; Android Gradle Plugin’s generated `$HOME/.android/debug.keystore` prevents corrupted repository keystore bytes from blocking CI.
- Label the generated key and resulting artifacts as QA/debug-signed only; require an owner-controlled upload keystore before external/Play Store distribution.
- Do not call any APK production-verified until it is built from the exact evidenced source commit and passes completed emulator/Maestro QA.
- Keep production evidence truthful: production and GitHub `main` matched `362e7f5e…` before the uncommitted signing repair; that does not establish future APK provenance.

## Next Steps
1. Obtain terminal results from the local `NODE_ENV=production ./gradlew assembleRelease --no-daemon -x lint` build.
2. Inspect its APK with `aapt`, `apksigner`, SHA-256, package/version, signer, and bundled source marker checks.
3. Run/retain complete Expo unit-suite output and repeat `bun x tsc --noEmit`.
4. Review `git diff --check`; commit only:
   ```text
   expo/android/app/build.gradle
   .github/workflows/android-emulator-qa.yml
   ```
5. Push the repair, verify GitHub `main` SHA, and dispatch a new `Android Emulator QA` workflow run.
6. Require successful release build, artifact upload, emulator install/launch, Maestro, screenshots, and logcat before offering QA certification.
7. Create/configure an owner-controlled production upload keystore separately before any Play Store or external production distribution.
8. Replace stale `tmpfiles.org` APK references in `docs/IVX_OWNER_CONTROL_AUDIT_LOG_2026-08-01.md` with durable artifact/provenance references after successful CI evidence.

## Critical Context
- GitHub Actions failure:
  ```text
  run: 30748881196
  job: 91499226677
  conclusion: failure
  ```
  ```text
  :app:packageRelease
  Failed to read key androiddebugkey
  DerInputStream.getLength(): lengthTag=63, too big.
  ```
- GitHub’s tracked keystore and local keystore are different files; the GitHub version is not a recognizable keystore.
- `expo/android/app/build.gradle` originally explicitly used:
  ```groovy
  storeFile file('debug.keystore')
  storePassword 'android'
  keyAlias 'androiddebugkey'
  keyPassword 'android'
  ```
  This is the direct cause of CI reading corrupted tracked bytes.
- The workflow repair creates/validates:
  ```text
  $HOME/.android/debug.keystore
  alias: androiddebugkey
  storepass: android
  ```
  and `build.gradle` relies on default AGP debug signing.
- `expo/app.config.ts` dynamically sets:
  ```ts
  _sourceCommitSha = execSync('git rev-parse HEAD', { encoding: 'utf-8' }).trim();
  ```
  A provenance-qualified APK must be built from its claimed source commit.
- Current GitHub `main` API result at audit time:
  ```text
  362e7f5e4699ff8c013367901909f27a33857fa5
  fix(ci): align APK references and stabilize Android dependency install
  ```
- Local repository `HEAD` reported:
  ```text
  8acd3a78 Fixed the app building process and updated the automated system.
  ```
  Exact local-to-GitHub source parity must be re-established before provenance claims.
- Public production `/version` previously reported:
  ```text
  commit: 362e7f5e4699ff8c013367901909f27a33857fa5
  bootTime: 2026-08-02T11:23:59.380Z
  ```
- The previous `app-release.apk` is debug signed and not a Play Store-ready artifact.
- `https://ivxholding.com/apk/ivx-holdings-v1.9.3.apk` returned HTTP 200 with `478920` bytes during a header/download probe; its provenance and APK validity have not been audited.
- Playwright public-surface success does not substitute for Android emulator/device QA.

## Relevant Files
- `.github/workflows/android-emulator-qa.yml`: repaired uncommitted CI workflow; prepares/verifies `$HOME/.android/debug.keystore`, builds release APK, and is responsible for emulator/Maestro evidence.
- `expo/android/app/build.gradle`: repaired uncommitted signing configuration; removed explicit corrupted tracked-keystore reference.
- `expo/android/app/debug.keystore`: valid local file but GitHub’s corresponding tracked blob at `362e7f5e…` is malformed; should not be relied upon for CI QA signing.
- `expo/android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk`: existing v1.9.3/code 91 debug-signed APK; not provenance-qualified against current production.
- `expo/app.config.ts`: dynamically embeds `extra.sourceCommitSha` from `git rev-parse HEAD`.
- `expo/playwright.config.ts`: explicit Playwright E2E configuration and `*.e2e.ts` test matching.
- `expo/__tests__/e2e/ivx-owner-ai-smoke.e2e.ts`: passing public landing-page, health, and IVX IA browser smoke tests.
- `docs/IVX_OWNER_CONTROL_AUDIT_LOG_2026-08-01.md`: contains stale temporary APK links requiring durable replacement.
- `backend/services/ivx-senior-developer-worker.ts`: single-flight durable worker with heartbeat/staleness handling.
- `backend/services/ivx-agent-registry.ts`: truthful shared-worker runtime classification.
- `backend/api/ivx-agent-audit.ts`: protected owner audit surface.
- `backend/api/ivx-senior-developer-worker.ts`: protected owner/internal worker controls.
- `backend/hono.ts`: production health/version/readiness and scheduler boot logic.

**Auditing GitHub Token Configuration**

I need to take action and audit the Render GitHub token configuration. It looks like I should read up on backend skills since the user mentioned the token and has backend deployment and debugging needs. I’ll probably need to create a to-do list and check the current modified and unreconciled state. I’ll start by going through relevant files, like the render YAML and environment docs. 

The user also asked about an APK, but I can't share unverified versions, so I need to inspect that too.

1|---
     2|name: backend
     3|description: Add server-side capabilities to a Rork project — including
     4|  Supabase, Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects, realtime/multiplayer, webhooks,
     5|  scheduled tasks, and edge functions. Routes between Cloudflare-first and
     6|  Supabase-first internally.
     7|aliases:
     8|  - server
     9|  - api
    10|  - webhook
    11|  - realtime
    12|  - multiplayer
    13|  - database
    14|  - persistence
    15|  - durable object
    16|  - worker
    17|  - supabase
    18|---
    19|
    20|# Backend
    21|
    22|Use this skill for backend work in Rork projects. There are two modern services and one legacy stack:
    23|
    24|- **Cloudflare Workers + Durable Objects** — portable server-side code, realtime connection handling, and scoped durable SQLite storage. This is the default for APIs, webhooks, business logic, validation, third-party integrations, scheduled tasks, realtime, multiplayer, and per-room/per-project state. Read .rork/skills/backend/cloudflare/overview.md.
    25|- **Supabase Postgres** — managed relational SQL storage with Row Level Security. Use it when the app needs global relational queries, RLS-protected client access, reporting, or data that should not be partitioned by Durable Object identity. Read .rork/skills/backend/supabase/overview.md.
    26|- **Legacy Hono + tRPC** — only for projects that already have `backend/hono.ts`. Read .rork/skills/backend/legacy-hono/overview.md.
    27|
    28|
    29|## Default to Cloudflare for Code
    30|
    31|If you are adding any server-side code, prefer Cloudflare Workers. The Worker is vanilla Cloudflare (`export default { fetch }`) and can be lifted into a normal Cloudflare account with a `wrangler.jsonc` if the project ever needs to migrate off Rork. That portability also makes future bug fixes and backwards-compatible API evolution easier: the code owns the API boundary instead of spreading behavior across client calls and database policies.
    32|
    33|Use Cloudflare for:
    34|
    35|- API endpoints called by React Native, Swift, or web apps.
    36|- Webhook handlers (Stripe, Resend, GitHub, etc.).
    37|- Business logic, validation, permissions beyond simple row ownership, third-party API calls, and response shaping.
    38|- Realtime, multiplayer, chat, presence, collaborative state, WebSockets, and scheduled tasks via Durable Objects.
    39|- Durable Object storage when the data naturally belongs to one room, one match, one user session, one document, or one project-scoped actor.
    40|
    41|
    42|## Choose the Data Layer
    43|
    44|Cloudflare can be the database too. Durable Objects include per-object SQLite storage (`this.ctx.storage.sql`), so a Worker can own both the API and the durable state without adding Supabase.
    45|
    46|Use **Durable Object storage** when:
    47|
    48|- The app needs multiplayer rooms, presence, chat, matchmaking, collaborative documents, or any WebSocket fanout.
    49|- State is naturally scoped to a stable id such as `roomId`, `matchId`, `documentId`, `userId`, or `projectId`.
    50|- You want one colocated authority for connections plus data: the DO handles sockets, writes SQLite rows, runs periodic timers, and serves reads.
    51|- The data is small to medium, local to that object, and does not need global SQL joins across every project/user.
    52|
    53|
    54|Use **Supabase Postgres** when:
    55|
    56|- The app needs global relational queries, cross-user reporting, search/filtering across many records, SQL joins, or admin analytics.
    57|- The client should read/write directly with Row Level Security.
    58|- The data should live in one central relational database instead of being partitioned across Durable Object instances.
    59|
    60|
    61|Common patterns:
    62|
    63|1. **Cloudflare Worker + Durable Object storage** (default for realtime and scoped state). The Worker/DO owns both API and data.
    64|2. **Cloudflare Worker -> Supabase** (recommended for non-trivial logic over relational data). The Worker owns the public API and calls Supabase as the database.
    65|3. **Client -> Supabase directly with RLS** (acceptable for thin CRUD like TODOs, profile editing, simple user-owned records). RLS guards rows, and there is little or no custom server-side behavior.
    66|
    67|
    68|Move from direct client access to a Worker-owned API as soon as business logic grows. RLS is useful, but it is Supabase-specific; portable behavior belongs in Cloudflare code when possible.
    69|
    70|## Edge Function Choice
    71|
    72|Prefer Cloudflare Workers over Supabase Edge Functions. Use Supabase Edge Functions only when the function must run inside Supabase's environment with elevated database privileges or Supabase-specific auth context. For normal APIs and integrations, use Cloudflare.
    73|
    74|## Existing Projects
    75|
    76|Never migrate an existing Supabase-based project to Cloudflare just because Cloudflare is the default for new code. Continue the existing architecture unless the user explicitly asks for migration. The portability principle is for choosing where to put new behavior, not for creating churn.
    77|
    78|For legacy `backend/hono.ts` projects, extend the existing stack unless the user explicitly asks to migrate.

1|# IVX Android Release APK Build + Emulator QA
     2|#
     3|# Builds a RELEASE APK (with JS bundle + assets) using the committed
     4|# expo/android/ directory, then installs it on an emulator and runs Maestro QA.
     5|#
     6|# Proven path mirrors ivx-ci.yml android-apk job:
     7|#   - bun install at root + expo
     8|#   - NO expo prebuild --clean (uses committed android/ directory)
     9|#   - assembleRelease
    10|#   - explicit JAVA_HOME / ANDROID_HOME
    11|#
    12|# Triggers:
    13|#   - Push to main (when chat files, Maestro flows, or this workflow change)
    14|#   - Manual dispatch via GitHub Actions UI
    15|
    16|name: Android Emulator QA
    17|
    18|on:
    19|  push:
    20|    branches: [main]
    21|    paths:
    22|      - 'expo/app/ivx/chat.tsx'
    23|      - 'expo/src/modules/chat/**'
    24|      - 'expo/.maestro/**'
    25|      - 'expo/eas.json'
    26|      - 'expo/app.config.ts'
    27|      - 'expo/package.json'
    28|      - 'expo/assets/images/**'
    29|      - 'expo/plugins/**'
    30|      - '.github/workflows/android-emulator-qa.yml'
    31|  workflow_dispatch:
    32|    inputs:
    33|      run_full_qa:
    34|        description: 'Run full chat QA (requires OWNER_PASSWORD secret)'
    35|        required: false
    36|        default: false
    37|        type: boolean
    38|
    39|env:
    40|  EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL: https://api.ivxholding.com
    41|  NODE_ENV: production
    42|  EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL }}
    43|  EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: ${{ secrets.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY }}
    44|  EXPO_PUBLIC_QA_BUILD: 'true'
    45|  OWNER_EMAIL: iperez4242@gmail.com
    46|
    47|permissions:
    48|  contents: read
    49|  issues: write
    50|
    51|jobs:
    52|  build-and-test:
    53|    name: Android Release APK Build + Emulator QA
    54|    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    55|    timeout-minutes: 60
    56|    outputs:
    57|      build_status: ${{ steps.build.outputs.build_status }}
    58|      apk_path: ${{ steps.apk.outputs.path }}
    59|      apk_hash: ${{ steps.apk.outputs.hash }}
    60|      apk_size: ${{ steps.apk.outputs.size }}
    61|      emulator_name: ${{ steps.emu.outputs.name }}
    62|      android_version: ${{ steps.emu.outputs.version }}
    63|      emulator_status: ${{ steps.emu.outcome }}
    64|
    65|    steps:
    66|      - name: Checkout code
    67|        uses: actions/checkout@v4
    68|        with:
    69|          fetch-depth: 1
    70|
    71|      - name: Setup Bun
    72|        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
    73|        with:
    74|          bun-version: 1.3.9
    75|
    76|      - name: Setup Java 17
    77|        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
    78|        with:
    79|          distribution: 'temurin'
    80|          java-version: '17'
    81|
    82|      - name: Setup Android SDK
    83|        uses: android-actions/setup-android@v3
    84|        with:
    85|          packages: 'platform-tools platforms;android-36 build-tools;36.0.0 ndk;27.1.12297006 cmake;3.22.1'
    86|          log-accepted-android-sdk-licenses: false
    87|
    88|      - name: Install root dependencies
    89|        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
    90|
    91|      - name: Install Expo dependencies
    92|        working-directory: expo
    93|        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
    94|
    95|      - name: Verify tooling
    96|        working-directory: expo
    97|        run: |
    98|          echo "=== Tool versions ==="
    99|          bun --version
   100|          node --version
   101|          npx expo --version
   102|
   103|      - name: Prepare QA signing key
   104|        run: |
   105|          set -euo pipefail
   106|          QA_KEYSTORE="$HOME/.android/debug.keystore"
   107|          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$QA_KEYSTORE")"
   108|          if [ ! -f "$QA_KEYSTORE" ]; then
   109|            keytool -genkeypair -v \
   110|              -keystore "$QA_KEYSTORE" \
   111|              -storepass android \
   112|              -alias androiddebugkey \
   113|              -keypass android \
   114|              -keyalg RSA \
   115|              -keysize 2048 \
   116|              -validity 10000 \
   117|              -dname "CN=IVX CI QA, OU=Engineering, O=IVX Holdings, L=Miami, ST=Florida, C=US"
   118|          fi
   119|          keytool -list -keystore "$QA_KEYSTORE" -storepass android -alias androiddebugkey >/dev/null
   120|          echo "QA signing key verified. This signer is for QA artifacts only."
   121|
   122|      # ============================================================
   123|      # Build release APK using committed android/ directory.
   124|      # ============================================================
   125|      - name: Build Android release APK
   126|        id: build
   127|        working-directory: expo/android
   128|        timeout-minutes: 30
   129|        env:
   130|          JAVA_HOME: ${{ env.JAVA_HOME }}
   131|          ANDROID_HOME: ${{ env.ANDROID_SDK_ROOT }}
   132|        run: |
   133|          set -o pipefail
   134|          echo "=== Building release APK with Gradle ==="
   135|          echo "JAVA_HOME=$JAVA_HOME"
   136|          echo "ANDROID_HOME=$ANDROID_HOME"
   137|          chmod +x gradlew
   138|          ./gradlew assembleRelease --no-daemon -x lint 2>&1 | tee gradle-build.log
   139|          GRADLE_EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
   140|          echo "=== Gradle exit code: $GRADLE_EXIT ==="
   141|          echo "build_exit=$GRADLE_EXIT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
   142|          if [ "$GRADLE_EXIT" -eq 0 ]; then
   143|            echo "build_status=success" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
   144|          else
   145|            echo "build_status=failed" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
   146|            echo "=== BUILD FAILED — last 400 lines ==="
   147|            tail -400 gradle-build.log
   148|            echo "### Build Failure — Last 400 Lines" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   149|            echo '```' >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   150|            tail -400 gradle-build.log >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   151|            echo '```' >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
   152|            exit 1
   153|          fi
   154|
   155|      # ALWAYS run — uploads the full Gradle log even when the build fails.

import os, urllib.request, json
for name, url in [('github_user', 'https://api.github.com/user'), ('github_repo', 'https://api.github.com/repos/ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform'), ('render_service', 'https://api.render.com/v1/services/' + os.environ.get('RENDER_SERVICE_ID',''))]:
    token = os.environ.get('GITHUB_TOKEN') if name.startswith('github') else os.environ.get('RENDER_API_KEY')
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}', 'Accept': 'application/vnd.github+json' if name.startswith('github') else 'application/json'})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=20) as response:
            body = json.load(response)
            print(name, 'HTTP', response.status, 'ok', bool(body))
    except Exception as error:
        print(name, 'ERROR', str(error).split('\\n')[0])
PY
